findings.text: Perf device ioctl entry first applies a write permission check, then acquires the event context lock, dispatches to the internal ioctl handler, releases the lock and returns its status. The compat variant rewrites the size field of four pointer carrying commands to native pointer size when the incoming size matches compat pointer size, otherwise delegates unchanged; on builds without compat support it is absent.

Task wide enable and disable walk the calling task owned event list under the task perf mutex, and for each event hold its context lock while applying the corresponding enable or disable operation to the event and its children before unlocking. Both report success in these fragments.
Global helper perf_allow_kernel decides whether kernel level capture is permitted by combining the paranoid level and monitor capability with the perf open security hook for kernel access.

Ring buffer reference helpers are globally visible: one obtains a referenced buffer for an event with redirection through the parent and safe handling of concurrent teardown, one drops a reference and defers reclamation until the last reference with a check that no events remain attached, and auxiliary release drops its own reference and invokes inner free only when last.

Attribute copy zeroes the destination, reads user size, substitutes version zero size when zero, rejects sizes outside version zero to page size, copies only the caller size with the struct copy helper, records size, reports oversize by writing back kernel structure size and returning too big, and rejects any nonzero reserved field.

Attribute validation masks sample type and read format against their maxima, validates branch bits against the branch maximum, requires at least one non privilege branch bit, propagates privilege bits from exclusion settings when none are set and updates the stored mask, and requires kernel permission when privileged branch bits are requested. Register masks are validated when requested, stack sampling requires architecture support plus an exclusive upper bound and eight byte alignment, max stack defaults from sysctl when zero, cgroup sampling is rejected without config support, weight modes are mutually exclusive, and combinations around inherit, exec behaviour and trap handling are rejected.

Filter string handling duplicates a user string bounded by page size, defaults to invalid argument, routes tracing events to the tracing filter setter while temporarily dropping the context mutex around that call, routes address filter capable events to the address filter setter, frees the copy and returns the setter status.

Address filter installation rejects child events, parses the string into a temporary list, asks the PMU to validate the list, atomically replaces the installed list, applies the new set to children, and on parse or validation failure discards the temporary list and clears the file filter count while propagating the error.

Filter text is duplicated then split on space comma and newline with empty tokens skipped; each definition starts with an action then a source and ends after source validation. Actions are filter start and stop. Sources carry an offset and optionally a size plus filename, with kernel versus file variants distinguished. Filter action requires nonzero size. File backed entries require a filename, require a per task context with cpu wide rejected as unsupported, resolve the path with follow semantics, require a regular file, and increment the file filter count. Successful entries reset tracking for the next definition; any violation discards all parsed entries and returns an error.

Output redirection to another event rejects self reference, requires equal CPU assignment, requires equal hardware target for per task buffers, requires equal clock, requires equal forward versus backward direction, and requires equal PMU when both sides generate auxiliary data. A null target clears redirection. Redirection is refused when the source has active mappings, when the target is revoked or earlier in lifecycle, when no buffer can be acquired, or when the target buffer lost its last mapping during the race.

Attachment warns on child events, removes any old buffer under its event lock with RCU list deletion while recording an RCU batch and marking pending, synchronizes only if a previous detach is pending before joining a new buffer, adds to the new buffer under its event lock with RCU list insertion, stops auxiliary producing events before swapping the buffer pointer, publishes the new pointer with RCU assignment, releases the old reference, and wakes waiters when a previous buffer was detached.

Mapping open increments event and buffer mapping counts, additionally counts auxiliary mappings when the offset is nonzero, and notifies the PMU mapped hook when present with lookup done under RCU and a single read of the PMU pointer. Mapping close notifies the unmapped hook, stops auxiliary output and frees auxiliary pages with memory accounting adjustments when the last auxiliary mapping closes, detaches the event when its last mapping closes, and when the buffer loses its last mapping repeatedly takes event references and detaches every redirecting event with restart on concurrent redirection before undoing data mapping accounting and releasing the buffer reference.

User page initialization runs under RCU, does nothing when no buffer is attached, otherwise marks bit zero deprecated, sets size to the offset of the reserved field, sets data offset to page size and sets data size from the buffer data size helper.

Auxiliary teardown releases PMU private state through its free callback when present then clears the callback and pointer, frees each auxiliary page after clearing its private flag, releases the page array and zeroes the page count, and warns if invoked in atomic context because the final release is expected from mapping close after stopping transactions.

Paused state clears only when unpausing a buffer that still has pages, otherwise it sets paused. Auxiliary presence is defined as nonzero auxiliary page count. New address filters are zero allocated on the node of the event CPU with fallback to node zero for per task events, initialized as list nodes and appended to the supplied list, returning null on allocation failure.

Address filter installation requires the caller to already hold the context mutex. Exchange of installed filters serializes list splicing with a raw spinlock with interrupts saved, then frees the old list outside the lock. Temporary parse lists need no locking because they are still private to the installer.

Tracing filter updates must not hold the context mutex while invoking the tracing filter setter because that path can deadlock against it; the caller temporarily releases the mutex and reacquires it afterwards, relying on an already held context reference and accepting that the event may migrate contexts without affecting tracing state.

Output redirection holds one or two mapping mutexes in address order with nesting annotation to serialize against mapping close, while buffer membership changes use the buffer event lock with interrupts disabled plus RCU list primitives and RCU pointer publish. Buffer lookup uses RCU read locking with reference acquisition that fails on zero, and mapping close combines auxiliary mutex, mapping mutex, RCU traversal, per event references and a restart loop to cope with concurrent redirection.

Task wide enable and disable nest per event context locks inside the caller task perf mutex. Device ioctl nests the internal operation inside the event context lock. Auxiliary stop iterates the buffer event list under RCU and invokes a per CPU stop helper, restarting the traversal when the target CPU reports retry.

Observed address filter state on an event comprises a list of filters, a lock protecting that list, and a count of file backed filters, with individual filters carrying an action, offset, size, path and list node. Management distinguishes parents which own filters from children which never own their own.

Observed ring buffer carries a user page pointer, page and mapping counts, lock and reference counts for data and auxiliary sides, an event list with its lock, pause flag, auxiliary page array with count and private state plus free callback, mapping user and offsets used for accounting. Observed event carries buffer pointer and membership node, RCU batch and pending flag, mapping count and mutex, wait queue, context pointer, parent link, CPU and on CPU identity, clock, direction flag, auxiliary capability, PMU pointer, hardware target and lifecycle state.

Observed mapping page exposes a deprecation flag for bit zero, structure size, data offset and data size. Observed attribute carries size, reserved fields, sample type with branch sample type plus register and stack sampling parameters and max stack depth, read format, and controls around inherit, thread inheritance, exec behaviour and trap handling.

Address filter parsing moves per definition from action state to source state to end state and back to action after validation, starting in action and requiring action on completion. An action token is accepted only in action state and a source token only in source state; reaching end triggers semantic checks and either commits the entry and resets kernel filename and filter tracking or aborts the whole parse.

Buffer membership pending state is set when detaching from an old buffer with the current RCU batch recorded, remains set across a null target, and is cleared by a conditional RCU wait immediately before joining a subsequent buffer, ensuring readers no longer reference the old membership before reuse.

Auxiliary and mapping memory moves from mapped to stopped to freed to unaccounted: last auxiliary unmap stops all producing events then frees pages and private state, last data unmap detaches redirecting events then undoes accounting and drops the final reference with deferred RCU reclamation. Paused flag and auxiliary presence gate transitions as described in invariants.

Holding the context mutex across the tracing filter setter risks deadlock, so the temporary release is required; implementers must tolerate event migration to another context during that window and must already hold a context reference.

Changing output while events run can lose data because auxiliary producers are stopped only at attach time and the pointer swap races with mapping close; checks for active mappings, revoked state and live buffer mapping count plus ordered double locking and wakeup after detach are required to avoid use after free and missed wakeups.

Freeing auxiliary memory in atomic context indicates a lifecycle violation because final release must follow transaction stop from mapping close. Address filter parsing must release duplicated filenames, original text and partially built entries on every error path and put resolved paths when discarding filters, otherwise it leaks memory and path references.

Attribute sizing and limits observed as interface facts: version zero attribute size as minimum and zero substitute, page size as maximum attribute size and as user filter bound and mapping page data offset, unsigned short maximum as exclusive upper bound for user stack size with eight byte alignment, and sysctl default for max stack when zero.

Sampling and lifecycle constants observed: sample type and read format maxima defining valid mask bits, branch sample maxima and privilege versus all privilege masks governing validation and permission checks, revoked state as cutoff for redirection eligibility, and compat handling for set filter, identifier, query BPF and modify attributes commands.

Error signalling observed: invalid argument for malformed input and rejected combinations, too big with size feedback for oversize attributes, no memory for allocation failure, operation not supported for cpu wide file filters, no such system when stack dump is unsupported on the build, access denied for unprivileged kernel capture, and retry handling for per CPU stop races.
